title: Rational projective-line preservation of constructible localizing categories
statement: Fix distinct primes $\ell,p$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ or the finite-subextension-valued $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}}_\ell$ of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], with pulled-back coefficients [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Put $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$, $W=P\times_Y P$, $q:P\to Y$, $p_1,p_2:W\to P$, and $\Delta:P\to W$, using [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Write $D(Z)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_Z})$ for the ordinary unbounded category, with the derived functors of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and tensor of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $\mathcal L_Z=\Loc(\Dbc(Z,\Lambda))$, where $\Dbc$ means bounded cohomology with finite constant local models as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and $\Loc$ is the full replete triangulated closure under all small ambient coproducts [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Use the positive Tate line $L_Z=\Lambda_Z(1)$ [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] and $T_Z(A)=(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}L_Z)[2]$ [def-sfb-tate-twisted-projection-comparison]. The schemes $Y,P,W$ are Noetherian and qcqs; $q,p_1,p_2,\Delta$ are proper, $\Delta$ is closed, its complementary open immersion $j:W\setminus\Delta(P)\to W$ is quasi-compact, and $\ell$ is invertible on these schemes. All schemes and arrows satisfy the standing setting. Each pullback and proper pushforward along $q,p_1,p_2,\Delta$ preserves the corresponding $\mathcal L$ and is exact. The coefficient unit and $L_Z$ belong to $\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$, $\mathcal L_Z$ is tensor-closed, and $T_Z$ preserves $\mathcal L_Z$. In particular $Rq_*:\mathcal L_P\to\mathcal L_Y$ and $T_Pq^*:\mathcal L_Y\to\mathcal L_P$ are well-defined exact functors. The preservation pair is the obligation named $\mathrm{localizingPreservation}$; the additional geometry and intermediate-functor assertions record its hypothesis checks.

source.note:
Construction material retained from the earlier split. The following proof-in-words was previously attached to this node. It is preserved here verbatim as source material for the worker who will prove the corresponding Lean declaration; this stage-1 node intentionally has no proof steps.

Former proof step 1:
Properness and Noetherianity. By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], $q$ is proper, and so are $p_1,p_2$, since each is the projective-line projection over $P$ (with the factors interchanged for $p_1$). By [def-weil-proper-morphism] they are separated and of finite type; thus the diagonal $\Delta$ of $q$ is closed. Clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] makes $\Delta$ proper. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] successively to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $q$ and $p_1$: $Y,P,W$ are Noetherian, hence locally Noetherian and quasi-compact.

Former uses: ["lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper", "def-weil-proper-morphism", "lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper", "lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian"]
Former elementary flag: False
Former source: {'document': 'literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-six-functors-basics/sk-prop-p1-adjunction-rational/sk-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-unit-counit.proof.md', 'place': 'Well-definedness (1): proper projections, closed diagonal; existing geometric tools'}

Former proof step 2:
Quasi-separatedness and the open complement. The existing Mathlib leaf [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] applies to each of the locally Noetherian schemes $Y,P,W$ from Step 1. Together with their quasi-compactness it proves they are qcqs. Put $j:W\setminus\Delta(P)\hookrightarrow W$. For any affine open $V\subseteq W$, the open subscheme $V\setminus\Delta(P)$ of the Noetherian scheme $W$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. This subscheme is $j^{-1}(V)$. Therefore $j$ is a quasi-compact morphism by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. These cited leaves supply the topological subclaims formerly proved inline, including the exact hypothesis required for open--closed exactness.

Former uses: ["lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated", "lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian", "def-weil-finite-type-morphism"]

Former proof step 3:
Standing geometric setting. The structure map $a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and of finite type by hypothesis. Clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] applied to $q,a_Y$, and then to $p_1,a_Yq$, makes $a_P=a_Yq$ and $a_W=a_Yqp_1$ separated and locally of finite type. Both maps are quasi-compact: the only opens of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are empty and the whole space, and their inverse images are empty or the quasi-compact schemes $P,W$ from Step 1. Thus both maps are of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Consequently $Y,P,W$ satisfy the separated-finite-type standing hypothesis in the later rational theorems; all displayed arrows are $k$-morphisms by the fibre-product construction. This argument does not require $Y$ proper over $k$.

Former proof step 4:
Coefficient convention. The integer $\ell$ is a unit on $Y,P,W$ and the open complement: its image is nonzero in the field $k$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, and structural ring maps carry units to units. This verifies the Tate-twist invertibility hypothesis. The fixed $E$ is a finite subextension of $\Qlb$, whose coefficient ring uses the finite-subextension-valued convention in the statement. The Cartesian-coefficient theorem [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies inverse images of these pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaves, and their Tate twists, with the corresponding coefficient sheaves. It also states that module pullback is exact inverse image. These are the coefficients used throughout the construction.

Former source: {'document': 'literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-six-functors-basics/sk-prop-p1-adjunction-rational/sk-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-unit-counit.proof.md', 'place': 'Well-definedness (1)--(3): Cartesian condensed coefficient system and twist hypotheses'}

Former proof step 5:
Domains of the functors. The category $\Dbc$ in this statement uses the finite constant local models of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: on each stratum its cohomology is locally obtained from a finitely presented scalar module by extension to the coefficient sheaf, and cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval. For these constant-model categories, [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] identifies $\Dctf$ with $\Dbc$ and their localizing closures. Its qcqs hypothesis holds for $Y,P,W$ by the preceding geometric and coefficient steps. Thus these are precisely the categories $\Loc(\Dctf)$ used in the enclosing unit. Pullbacks preserve these closures and are exact by [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback]. Proper pushforwards preserve them and are exact by [det-proper-image-localizing-proper], including $Rq_*,Rp_{i*},R\Delta_*$. Closure under derived tensor is [det-thm-sf-pf-field-tensor]. The coefficient sheaf is a rank-one free module, and the Tate sheaf is locally free of rank one by [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], so each has the finite constant local model with scalar module $\Lambda(*)$ on a single stratum in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: on a trivializing cover the model is $\Lambda_U\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}\Lambda(*)\simeq\Lambda_U$. The scalar module $\Lambda(*)$ is free of rank one over itself, hence finitely presented. Concentrated in degree zero, they therefore belong to $\Dbc$. Consequently tensoring by the Tate sheaf and shifting also preserve these closures. This checks the domain of each object in the diagonal, exchange and trace constructions, including unbounded objects in the localizing closure.

Thus the composite q^* followed by tensor with the positive Tate line and [2] is exact as well. Its underlying object formula is precisely the fixed twist of [def-sfb-tate-twisted-projection-comparison]; no adjunction with Rq_* is asserted here.

proof.text: The projective-line projection is proper, and both self-product projections are proper by base change. Its relative diagonal is closed and hence proper. Finite type over Spec k makes Y, P and W locally Noetherian; quasi-compactness makes them Noetherian. Their open complement is quasi-compact. Compositions give all standing separated finite-type structure maps. Distinct primes make ell a unit in k and hence in every residue field by the structural ring maps. These are exactly the fields of the unchanged geometry package.

The localizing closure existence theorem gives the inherited triangulated structures. An ambient exact functor that preserves the underlying object predicates lifts to an exact functor on the full subcategories by Mathlib ObjectProperty.isTriangulated_lift. The existential shift structures in LocalizingFunctorChecks are the same structures used to prove ambient exactness. Composition combines preservation and ambient exactness, and the same lifting theorem supplies the exact restriction.

For the chosen finite-extension or finite-subextension-valued closure coefficient, Dctf and Dbc have equal localizing closures. Apply the existing unbounded pullback theorem, and transport its localizing object assertion through this equality. For each proper map, the coefficient-specific proper-image theorem supplies constructibility and sum preservation; the general proper localizing restriction theorem supplies preservation. Ambient derived pushforward is triangulated. The preceding lifting argument produces LocalizingFunctorChecks in each case.

The existing rank-one regular scalar model proves bounded constructibility of the coefficient unit. The positive Tate-line generator theorem gives bounded constructibility of the line using the common-root cover and finite scalar models. The field tensor theorem gives tensor closure. The line therefore belongs to the localizing closure, so tensor with it preserves that closure, as does shift by two. Use the native derived tensor shift and triangulated instances and the lifting argument to obtain exact twist restrictions.

Specialize the pullback and proper-pushforward checks to q, the two projections, and the diagonal, with their actual structural maps and IsOver equations. Specialize the object checks to Y, P and W. Compose pullback along q with the positive twist on P, then assemble the unchanged ProjectiveLineLocalizingChecks structure.
